questions.stem_text: Which culture lived a primarily sedentary lifestyle in the Southwest?
questions.answer_explanation: The Mogollon culture is recognized for its development of agriculture and permanent settlements in the Southwest, distinguishing them as a primarily sedentary society in contrast to the nomadic lifestyles of neighboring cultures.

questions.stem_text:
Analysis of the teeth of a hominid species discovered in Malapa Cave in South Africa,
dating just after 2 million years ago, indicates a diet that consisted primarily of:

options.B: primarily C 3 plants that included barley and oats.
options.C: large quantities of insects and small mammals.
options.D: a balanced diet of fruits, vegetables, meat, and fish.
options.E: primarily C 4 plants that included corn and potatoes.

questions.answer_explanation: The analysis of the teeth of the hominid species indicates adaptations for processing a varied diet, including the consumption of meat and fish, supported by isotopic evidence and dental morphology that suggest a reliance on both animal proteins and plant materials.

questions.stem_text:
The Gault site in south-central Texas has produced evidence from 13,000 years ago that
Paleoindians chose this location based on the:

options.A: nearness of the site to navigable rivers and the Gulf coast.
options.C: presence of a large lake for fishing and transportation.
options.D: nearby location of migratory routes of large mammals such as bison.
options.E: proximity to a local source of chert for quarrying and making stone tools.

questions.answer_explanation: The Gault site is significant because it demonstrates that Paleoindians strategically selected locations with easy access to chert deposits, which were essential for crafting durable stone tools necessary for their survival and daily activities.

questions.stem_text:
Tiwanaku, with its capital at Titicaca, was one of the ___________ kingdoms of the ancient
world.
questions.answer_explanation: Tiwanaku, known for its impressive monuments and extensive agricultural systems, was one of the largest and most influential civilizations in the Andean region, demonstrating significant urban development and political organization in the ancient world.

questions.stem_text: When did Aborigines occupy the harsh interior of Australia?
questions.answer_explanation: The correct answer is 40,000-45,000 years ago because archaeological evidence, including ancient tools and art, indicates that Aboriginal Australians have inhabited the interior of Australia for this extensive period, showcasing their adaptation to harsh environments.
